column2: req_desc

Station availability
GET /api/sites/{site_id}/availability returns every station of the site for one site-local date with its booked, buffer, own and not-on-the-clock sectors, each buffer sized by the station's kind, as defined in API and Business rules.

Burner Dial drag claim
Dragging clockwise by pointer or touch from an open point on a station's dial draws a claim arc that snaps to the booking step and stops where its own sanitation buffer would meet the next occupied sector, at the end of the day or at the member's available pack hours, shows the start, end and pack hours after this claim in the centre, never scrolls the page while a touch claim is in progress, and creates a hold on release under a fresh idempotency key, as qualified in Interactions.

Keyboard dial control
Each dial's Start time and End time spinbuttons move the window by a quarter hour with arrow keys and by an hour with Shift and an arrow key, drive the same arc, and let the member hold, confirm and release a window without a pointer, as qualified in Interactions.

Server hold
POST /api/bookings with an Idempotency-Key creates a held booking that moves its hours from available to committed and carries a server-set expiry instant, and refuses a member's fourth live hold with 422 hold_limit, as defined in API and Business rules.

Next-day cutoff
The server refuses a booking for the site's current or an earlier date, or for the site's next date once the site's own clock reaches the cutoff in Business rules, whatever time zone the browser uses.

Claim-to-ticket journey
A member drags a window on a dial while the dials keep reloading, confirms the hold, and sees the arc turn to the confirmed state, the centre numeral settle to the server balance and a new ticket on top of the spike.

One winner per window
Of several simultaneous claims that overlap one station's window or its sanitation buffer exactly one succeeds and every other answers 409 slot_taken with no ledger movement, and one member's simultaneous claims on different stations are judged one after another against that member's balance and hold limit.

Hold expiry
A held booking that reaches its hold_expires_at unconfirmed is expired on the server, returns its hours to the lots it drew from in one hold_release by Pilotlight, frees its window, and refuses a later confirm with 409 hold_expired, as defined in Business rules.

Hold and rejection display
A held window shows a pulsing outline and a countdown measured to the server's hold expiry on the server clock, never the browser's, and a rejected or expired claim snaps the arc back to zero length while the Booking status region announces the reason copy from Feedback states.

Lost-race journey
When two members claim the same last blast-chiller window, the loser's arc snaps back, the conflict is announced, and the loser's displayed pack hours equal their balance before the drag.

Booking state machine
Booking status changes only along the legal transitions in Business rules, exactly one of several simultaneous transitions on one booking commits, and every other transition is refused with the 409 the state machine gives without changing the booking or the ledger.

Cancellation forfeit window
Cancelling a held booking returns its hours, and cancelling a confirmed booking, by its member or by a kitchen manager of its site, refunds all, splits or forfeits its quarter hours by elapsed notice as defined in Business rules, with the refunded and forfeited hours stated in the response.

Cancel journey
From a ticket the member opens the cancel dialog, sees the hours that will be refunded and forfeited before confirming, keeps the dialog open while that outcome changes in place as the notice crosses an edge, and once the server answers sees the ticket marked Cancelled and the balance updated, or, when the booking was already cancelled elsewhere, the ticket redrawn as cancelled by that person.

Weekly series
POST /api/recurring-series books every occurrence of a weekly slot as a confirmed booking in one all-or-nothing step, or books nothing and names the conflicting or uncovered dates.

Wall-clock anchoring
Every occurrence of a weekly series keeps the same site-local start and end times across daylight-saving changes, costs its elapsed hours, and follows the published rule for missing and repeated local times.

Weekly slot journey
From a dial the member opens Repeat weekly, chooses the number of weeks while the preview follows, books the series, and sees one ticket per occurrence in the spike.

Paired hour ledger
Every change to a member's pack hours is one ledger movement of two entries that cancel out, a partial cancellation is one refund movement and one forfeit movement whose hours add up to the booking, entries are never edited or deleted, and the reported balances always equal the sums of their entries.

Atomic pack purchase
Buying a pack records the Kill Bill purchase, the ledger credit and one receipt email together, and while billing is unreachable it answers 503 and records none of them.

Purchase replay safety
A repeated pack purchase with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the original response without a second charge, and the same key with a different body answers 409 idempotency_conflict.

Buy-pack journey
A member opens a pack's dialog, pays, and sees the available pack hours rise, the new pack's line in the pack hours by expiry list and a pack-purchase line at the top of the hour ledger table, as qualified in Interactions.

Upload type and size limits
Compliance uploads are accepted only as PDF, PNG or JPEG files within the file size limit in Server boundary, and every other file, SVG included, is refused with the statuses in API.

Document and stored file together
A document record exists exactly when its stored object exists, no later upload or review removes or replaces an earlier document's object, and while storage is unreachable an upload answers 503 and leaves neither.

Own records only
A member can open only their own documents, document files, bookings and truck log, and another member's id answers 404 exactly as an unknown id does.

Document review
A kitchen manager verifies or rejects each pending document of members homed at their site, and verifying sets that member's valid-through date for the document's type as defined in Business rules.

Insurance valid-through edge
The server accepts holds, confirmations and series occurrences only while the member's certificate of insurance is valid now in the booking site's time zone and its valid-through date is on or after every booked date, and refuses the rest with certificate_expired whatever the client sends.

Expiry notices
Each member's document type with a valid-through date receives at most one 14-day notice and one 3-day notice email per valid-through date, judged on the member's home site's calendar as defined in Business rules.

Compliance journey
A member uploads a certificate of insurance and sees it waiting for review only once the server has answered, a kitchen manager opens and verifies it, and the member's coverage list then shows the new valid-through date.

Check-in window
A kitchen manager can check in a confirmed booking only inside the check-in window and while the member's certificate of insurance is valid, and otherwise gets 409 too_early, 409 too_late or 422 certificate_expired as defined in Business rules.

No-show marking
A kitchen manager can mark a confirmed booking as a no-show only from the time set in Business rules, which forfeits its committed hours in one ledger movement.

Manager site scope
A kitchen manager sees and acts on the bookings, documents, members and trucks of their own site only, and another site's ids answer 404.

Site day journey
A kitchen manager opens the site day board, checks in an arriving member, marks a missing one as a no-show while the board keeps reloading itself, and sees each row's status and actions change and the Site day status copy exactly as published in Feedback states.

Late check-out hours
At check-out, the whole minutes past the booked end at the commit instant are rounded to quarter hours as defined in Business rules, drawn from the member's available pack hours first in the lot order of DP-69, and any remainder becomes overage.

Overage amount
The overage subtotal, sales tax and total are computed once at check-out in whole cents with the rounding rule in Business rules, then stored and returned unchanged.

Overage billing record
A check-out whose overage total is above zero creates exactly one Kill Bill invoice on the member's account whose amount equals the overage total to the cent, committed as DP-79 requires, and while billing is unreachable a first check-out answers 503 and the booking stays checked in.

Late check-out journey
A kitchen manager checks out a late member through the check-out dialog and then sees the late hours, pack hours applied, overage total and their own name on that booking's row.

Truck visit recording
A kitchen manager records a truck's arrival and then its departure with the services performed and the operator's typed signature, with at most one open visit per truck.

Return gap flag
Each visit is flagged when its departure comes more than the return interval in Business rules after the previous departure, and every visits response states whether the truck is overdue, judged only on the server clock at the moment of that request.

Visit log journey
A kitchen manager finds an overdue truck through member search, records its arrival and departure, and sees the new visit at the top of the visit log with any gap flag and the Overdue notice gone.

Inspector link issue
Issuing an inspector link stores a PDF snapshot of the truck's log, emails the link to the inspector and returns a link that expires after the configured period, or answers 503 and does none of these while storage is unreachable.

Read-only scoped view
An inspector link exposes only the named truck's visit-log fields listed in API, never another member's data, and refuses every request other than GET with 405.

Revoke and reissue
Revoking a link stops it at once, reissuing replaces it with a new link and stops the old one, and revoked or expired links answer 410.

Inspector journey
An inspector opens the emailed link, sees the truck's visits with flagged gaps, downloads the PDF, and sees the expired or revoked heading exactly as published once the link is dead.

Effective-dated rates
A network finance lead schedules a site rate from a date after that site's own current date, rates are never edited, and a second rate for the same site and date answers 409 rate_exists.

Rate at booking start
A check-out's overage uses the rate whose effective date is the latest on or before the booking's site-local start date, even when a newer rate has taken effect since, and never a rate effective after that date.

Rate schedule journey
The finance lead picks a site, sees the Effective from field start on that site's next local date, schedules a new hourly rate and sales tax rate, and sees it in the rate schedule table marked Upcoming alongside the Current rate, with the table always showing the site picked last.

Utilisation report and export
The finance lead's monthly report and its CSV export give identical per-site hours and overage totals, counted by site-local month with pack expiry left out of forfeited hours, as defined in API.

Tenant-scoped search and totals
Member search, report totals, exports and the audit trail include only the signed-in user's incubator, so another incubator's members, hours, revenue and events never appear.

Tenant boundary on ids
Every route answers 404 to a caller whose role may use it for another incubator's site, station, pack, booking, document, member, truck, visit or inspector link id.

Reports journey
The finance lead chooses a month, optionally narrows the report to one member picked from search, reads the per-site table, and downloads the CSV.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on the port set in Deployment, and GET /api/health answers as defined in Deployment.

Sign-in and sessions
Seeded users sign in with email and password, receive the session and CSRF cookies defined in Business rules, land on the address they opened when their role has that screen and otherwise on their role's home, see their role's navigation (behind a Menu button at phone widths), sign out, and are returned to the sign-in form at the same address when their session ends, as qualified in Interactions.

Error shape and precedence
Every error response except the health check's 503 uses the single error body, and every API error follows the single precedence order defined in API.

Server boundary
The server accepts writes only from its own origin, enforces the content-type and body-size limits, and never serves source files or credentials, as defined in Server boundary.

Notification emails
Each event in the email list in Services sends exactly one message with the stated recipient and subject from the configured sender, even when a request is replayed, two reissues race or several server processes share the database.

Responsive layout
Every screen follows its layout band from Screens and layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal scrolling and every control at least 44 px in both directions as measured in Visual design.

Dialog focus and Escape
Every dialog moves focus inside when it opens, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab within it, closes on Escape and returns focus to the control that opened it, except where Interactions names another target.

Motion and reduced motion
Each motion completes within the durations in Motion and effects, and with reduced motion requested arcs, numerals and tickets jump to their final values, the hold outline stays steady and the hold countdown shows whole minutes only.

Stainless ticket look
The screens use the stainless palette, condensed display type, hairline steel rules between station rows and order-ticket cards with a torn edge and mono numerals described in Visual design.

Burner Dial craft
Each dial reads as a 24-hour ring whose hatched, dotted, flame and green sectors, centre readout and hold outline are legible and distinct from one another on a still screenshot.

Provider wiring from environment
Source reads every service URL and credential from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and makes real Kill Bill, S3 and SMTP calls rather than local stand-ins.

Attributed ledger movements
Every ledger movement and every check-in, no-show, check-out and cancellation records at write time the person who caused it, or the server for hold expiry, pack expiry and opening balances, that attribution never changes, and the hour ledger shows it.

Check-out replay safety
POST /api/bookings/{id}/check-out requires an Idempotency-Key, a replay returns the stored result without calling Kill Bill even while billing is unreachable, and each booking has at most one overage invoice, as defined in API and Business rules.

Only published fields are accepted
Every JSON and multipart request body accepts only the fields its endpoint lists for the caller's role, and any other field is refused with 422 validation naming it, with nothing stored.

Private data never reaches copies
Inspector link emails, visit-log PDFs and the inspector view carry only the published truck-log fields, never user emails, balances, booking references, internal ids or another truck's or member's data, and the inspector page requests only its own API paths, as defined in Business rules and Interactions.

Report URL is state
The report month and member filter live in the /reports address, so opening it directly or through sign-in, reloading it, or going Back and Forward restores the same fields, table and CSV link, as qualified in Interactions.

Hold replay safety
A repeated hold with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored 201 before any rule or contention check, writes no booking or movement and never counts toward the hold limit, and the same key with a different body or while still in flight answers 409, as defined in Business rules.

Manager cancellation
A kitchen manager of the booking's site can cancel a confirmed booking on the member's behalf with a required reason, under the normal forfeit split judged on the notice when the cancellation commits and attributed to that manager, while a member sending a reason, a finance lead and another site's manager are refused as defined in API, and a booking already cancelled elsewhere answers 409 invalid_transition.

Pack hour lots and expiry
Each purchase's hours form a lot valid through its home-site local purchase date plus 60 days, available hours always equal the sum of lot remainders, each lot carries a server-decided expiring_soon flag, and expired hours leave in exactly one pack-expiry movement from the home site's midnight, as defined in Business rules.

Lot drawing and return order
Debits draw lots earliest valid-through first with the opening balance last, releases and refunds return hours to the lots the booking drew latest valid-through first, and each movement and the Packs list, refreshed as stated in Interactions, show the lot allocation.

Role-shaped projections
Every JSON response carries exactly its published keys at every depth, so actor objects, member search, booking lists and other members' dial sectors carry no identifying or private fields beyond their shapes, and no response other than GET /api/me and the POST /api/session success carries a user's email address.

Rate resolution by site-local start date
The overage rate is resolved when the check-out commits, from the rate schedule as it stands then, so a rate scheduled after the booking but effective on or before its start date applies, and rate dates and states are judged on each site's own local date.

Server-decided overdue notice
While Trucks with a truck loaded, Truck log or the inspector view stays open, its Overdue notice follows only the overdue field of that screen's own visits request, repeated on the schedule in Interactions and never derived from the browser clock or time zone.

Live cancellation outcome
An open Cancel booking dialog, the member's or the kitchen manager's, rewrites its refund and forfeit sentence in its Cancellation outcome status in place within the delay stated in Interactions when the notice crosses the 72-hour or 48-hour edge, writing it only when the outcome changes and keeping the dialog open, focus and the typed reason.

Dial state survives reloads
The dial's regular and post-action reloads replace sectors only and keep the claim arc, spinbutton values, an in-progress drag, an open dialog with its values, focus, the Booking status text and the hold countdown, except that a window the reload shows as blocked snaps back and announces the slot_taken copy, as qualified in Interactions.

Tickets and rows follow the server
No ticket, Site day row or displayed balance changes before the server answers an action on it, and a 409 invalid_transition or hold_expired answer re-requests that booking, and for a member the ledger, and redraws only that ticket or row from the server, as qualified in Interactions.

Server-decided pack expiry on Packs
While Packs stays open it re-requests the ledger once a minute and redraws its numerals, pack hours by expiry list and hour ledger table from the response, so an expired lot's line leaves within 61 seconds after the home site's midnight and never before, and each line's flame marker comes only from the lot's expiring_soon field, never from the browser clock.

Documents stored as submitted
Each document response carries the sha256 of the exact uploaded bytes, and its file download, ETag and stored object match the uploaded file byte for byte in every status, rejected included, as defined in API and Server boundary.

Site day state survives reloads
Site day reloads its bookings for the shown date every 30 seconds and after each action, bringing in bookings made elsewhere, while keeping an open Check out dialog with its idempotency key, an open Cancel booking dialog with its typed reason and caret, focus and the Site day status text, as qualified in Interactions.

Committed overage invoice
An overage invoice is recorded only once Kill Bill reports it COMMITTED with exactly one external charge item carrying the published description and amount, it is never left as a draft, and any invoice created before a Kill Bill failure is voided before the 503, as defined in Services.

Latest site wins on Rates
On Rates the rate schedule table and the Effective from field always show the site chosen last, and a late answer for an earlier site, whether a schedule load or a Schedule rate response, never redraws them, as qualified in Interactions.

Exact layout bands
Each screen uses the phone layout below 640 px wide, the tablet layout from 640 to 1023 px and the desktop layout from 1024 px, exactly at those edges, as defined in Screens and layout.

Collapsed navigation is unavailable
Below 640 px wide the Main navigation sits behind a header Menu button whose aria-expanded tracks it, and while collapsed its links are absent from the accessibility tree, unfocusable, unclickable and take no space, as qualified in Interactions.

Latest rail choice wins on Book
On Book each change of site, date or station type makes every earlier availability request stale, so only the latest rail subject's dials are ever drawn, the dials are busy and unclaimable while its request is pending, and an outstanding claim attempt still completes, as qualified in Interactions.

Hold expiry takes effect at its instant
A held booking is expired from exactly its millisecond hold_expires_at on every server process, so from that instant its window is free, it no longer counts toward the hold limit, confirm answers 409 hold_expired and its single hold_release is committed before any response depends on it, while one millisecond earlier it is still live and confirmable.

Live series preview
The Repeat weekly dialog lists every occurrence with its elapsed hours in the site's time zone and shows the series total and remaining pack hours, updated in place within 100 ms of every Number of weeks change without any request, as qualified in Interactions.

Buy dialog survives Packs refresh
An open Buy dialog keeps one idempotency key until it closes or succeeds, including across a 401 resumed through Sign in again, the once-a-minute ledger refresh never closes it, moves focus, re-enables its pending button or writes Pack status, and a ledger answer requested before the latest balance-carrying response never rolls the balances back, as qualified in Interactions.

Storage-confirmed documents
A document row is committed only after storage acknowledges its object and a HEAD confirms its length, content type and sha256 and document-id metadata, any mismatch or storage error deletes the object and answers 503, and the Documents screen shows no row until the server answers and keeps the chosen file after a 503, as defined in Services and Interactions.

Keyboard site day
A kitchen manager runs Site day entirely by keyboard, with the published Tab order, pending row buttons that stay focused and aria-disabled, and focus moving after each answer as qualified in Interactions.

Inspector view layout bands
The inspector view uses its published desktop, tablet and phone arrangement exactly at the 640 px and 1024 px edges, with labelled visit cards on phones, no horizontal scrolling and a Download PDF link at least 44 by 44 px, as defined in Screens and layout.

Latest report query wins
On Reports the Member listbox only ever shows matches for the current text and a report answer for anything but the latest load never redraws the table, Report status, Month, Member or Download CSV link, so quick Back and Forward steps end matching the final address, as qualified in Interactions.

Session rotation, expiry and revocation
Sign-in issues a fresh session value that replaces the one the request carried, sessions expire after the idle and absolute limits, sign-out destroys the session idempotently, a fourth live session destroys the oldest, and dead values answer 401 with the codes in Business rules.

Indistinguishable credentials and throttled sign-in
An unknown email and a wrong password answer identically, repeated failures per email or per client address answer 429 too_many_attempts with Retry-After even for the correct password, and passwords are stored only as salted argon2id or bcrypt cost ≥10 hashes, as defined in Business rules.

Double-submit CSRF token
Every state-changing request from a signed-in session must carry an X-CSRF-Token header equal to that session's pl_csrf cookie or it answers 403 csrf_failed and changes nothing, judged after the origin and session checks and before the role check, as defined in Server boundary.

Inert stored text and security headers
Stored reasons, signatures, inspector emails and file names render as literal text everywhere, every response carries the published security headers, and every HTML page carries the published content security policy and no inline script, as defined in Server boundary.

Injection-safe ids, queries and search
Ids not in the published shape answer 404, malformed fields answer 422 naming them, injection payloads in any id, query or body field are treated as plain text with no 500 and no change, and member search matches percent, underscore and backslash characters literally, as defined in API.

Verified upload content
A file part is accepted only when its declared type is PDF, PNG or JPEG and its leading bytes match that declared type, and it is stored under a server-chosen key that never uses the submitted file name, as defined in Server boundary.

Append-only audit trail
Every write request to the API appends exactly one audit event with its actor and outcome, refusals included, which kitchen managers and finance leads read through GET /api/audit within their scope and which is never edited or deleted, as defined in API and Business rules.

Secrets stay server-side
No response, asset, error or audit event contains a configured secret, unexpected failures answer the exact opaque 500 body, and every endpoint enforces its roles on the server whatever the navigation shows, as defined in API and Server boundary.
/app/run.json exists, is valid JSON with exactly the string fields _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve, and the app is started only through it.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package with its version and licence; shipped packages are the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, plus the bundled fonts.
Every shipped package (as defined in IF-02) is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0, and every font under OFL-1.1.

The app stores data only in PostgreSQL, Kill Bill and the S3 bucket, with no SQLite, no Redis, no in-memory store standing in for the database (sessions, throttles and idempotency records included), and no files on disk as a datastore.
The provided development service configuration and its seeded credentials are left unchanged.
Fonts and icons are bundled and served by the app, and the built pages load nothing from third-party hosts.
Application source, server and client, is written in TypeScript; the only JavaScript files are build output and tool configuration.
